newsitem.title: GERMANY: Boss sees higher 1997 sales, profits.
newsitem.headline: Boss sees higher 1997 sales, profits.

text.p: German mens fashion house Hugo Boss AG said on Tuesday it expected sales and profit both to climb by around five percent this year.

Newly-appointed chief executive Joachim Vogt, in remarks he was due to give to the company's annual general meeting, said he expected sales to climb to 1.05 billion marks this year from 995 million marks last year.
Net profits should increase to 68.5 million marks from a year earlier figure of 64.9 million marks. Pre-tax profits should climb to 132 million marks from 125 million, he said.
Vogt said Boss would open 44 new stores by the end of this year, in around two months show a new mens collection, and offer its first women's range under the brand name "Hugo-woman" early next year.
